A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Person2Drive, despite v2's changed title. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and supplementary materials are readable and support reliable matching across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original driving-style evaluation, reward-model experiments, personalization results, closed-loop driving tests, and cross-scene analyses in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds category-level comparison models, Bench2Drive safety results, per-driver statistics, and an indicator-count ablation.

M1.justification: The DiffusionDrive backbone, three-stage PDSA procedure, style reward model, and head-only fine-tuning remain. V1 already documented the MLP architecture and combined trajectory/style losses in its supplement. V2 clarifies BEV feature integration without establishing a changed algorithm or new component.

E1.justification: V2 extends driving-safety evaluation to diverse, difficult Bench2Drive cases in Section 5.2/Table 6; v1 used Bench2Drive for base-model training but reported this evaluation only on Person2Drive. StyleDrive and the four Person2Drive routes remain. Increasing driver counts does not establish a new population or task.

E2.justification: Section 4.4/Table 5 introduces three Aggressive/Normal/Conservative group-trained comparison models, adding a substantive category-level alternative to individual personalization. V2 also adds PDSA-WB to the Person2Drive safety comparison and removes the former GT reference row. The existing StyleDrive comparator set is retained when moved into the main text.

E3.justification: Person2Drive expands from 30 to 50 participants and 33.3 to 55.5 driving hours, while retaining four routes and the same repetition allocation. New experiments introduce driver-to-category model matching and comparisons using 6–14 indicators. KL is now specified as symmetric rather than directed, a reported metric-specification revision that does not establish whether earlier experiments were recomputed.

E4.justification: V2 adds indicator-count sensitivity analysis (supplementary Table 8), per-driver gain analysis (Table 4), and broader safety analysis including difficult Bench2Drive cases and the without-BEV variant (Table 6). Existing cross-scene analyses and first-person qualitative cases remain. V1's separate top-down trajectory example is removed.

E5.justification: Beyond the retained cross-scene mean-and-variance reporting, v2 Table 4 adds per-driver gain means, variances, and percentages benefiting. Section 4.3 newly reports Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with p<0.001, introducing inferential support for the central personalization comparison. Neither version establishes repeated-training seed counts or an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Reported PDSA average Person2Drive MMDSS changes from 0.6840 to 0.6800 (Table 4), and its driving score changes from 72.78 to 70.13 (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 6). Person2Drive style-evaluation values, Figure 3 reward-model results, and Figure 4 indicator rankings also change. ANC, Bench2Drive, and indicator-count results are added. These are updated or additional results, not controlled evidence of a version-to-version performance loss. Matched StyleDrive and cross-scene tables retain their values.

T1.justification: V2 corrects Equation 1 by squaring the centered deviations inside the standard-deviation expression. Supplementary Equation 4 newly defines MMDdiff as MMDintra minus MMDinter for the indicator-count analysis. The existing MMD and MMDSS equations remain, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central dataset/platform, quantitative style evaluation, and lightweight personalization contributions remain. V2's abstract extends the performance-preservation claim explicitly to challenging scenarios. Its emphasis on plug-and-play, head-only adaptation largely restates a capability already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly limits demonstrated applicability to DiffusionDrive and explains that preliminary alternatives had unstable closed-loop behavior. It adds interpretations favoring individual over category-level supervision and supporting ten style indicators. The existing limitation that safety overrides suppress style expression remains.

D1.justification: V2 newly explains global BEV encoding and injection at each trajectory time step, and specifies histogram KL estimation with 50 bins, independent min–max normalization, and 10^-8 smoothing. It also clarifies automated labeling and route-level normalization. Existing MLP, sensor, hardware, and safety-controller details are retained; code and data release remains promised after acceptance.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 34 works. V2 adds the positioning statement that most personalized-driving methods are unsuitable for fully end-to-end deployment and no longer describes MAVERIC as end-to-end. These are limited substantive positioning changes; reference reordering and formatting do not add literature coverage.

P1.justification: The title changes from Driving with A Thousand Faces to Driving Like Yourself. V2 refines terminology and several explanatory paragraphs, separates supplementary collection protocol from dataset description, and moves existing StyleDrive and qualitative analyses into the main narrative. The overall section sequence and much of the prose remain.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two-column to single-column layout and redraws Figure 1. It converts the former Person2Drive evaluation table into Figure 2(b), substantially expands Table 4, restructures the safety table, and adds comparison and ablation tables. Existing supplementary displays move into the main text, while v1 Figure 5 is removed.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's mainly variant-based comparisons, v2's category-level controls directly strengthen the case for individual personalization. Per-driver statistical reporting, broader safety evaluation, the corrected Equation 1, and explicit single-backbone limitations improve assessability. The gain is limited by incomplete specification of the new evaluations and the MMD-versus-similarity ambiguity in supplementary Equation 4/Table 8, which weakens interpretation of the added indicator ablation.
